title: DiscoveryRootSkillPackage
description: Canonical instruction-only Agent Skill package published in a skill discovery root. It is a standalone package: it carries its own identity, version, and complete file inventory, and it is not an executable Agent Program package and is not carried inside one. A skill carried inside an executable package is the separate `apxm.package-local-skill` contract, which states a different constraint block rather than weakening this one. This schema also owns the shared skill definitions both contracts reference: `SkillMetadata`, `ResourceEntry`, and the two `instruction_source` branches.

instruction_source.description: Where this skill's instructions live. A discovery-root skill is standalone: it has no Agent Program source bundle for instructions to be part of, so only the file-carried `entry` branch is admissible here. The `kind` discriminant is still on the wire, so a document declaring `inline` is rejected rather than silently reinterpreted.

resources.description: The complete file inventory of the standalone package, including the instruction entry itself. A discovery-root skill's `package_digest` is taken over exactly this set.

executable_package.description: A discovery-root skill is not an executable Agent Program package. Its package-local sibling replaces this key with `carried_by_executable_package`, which asserts the opposite relationship rather than negating this one.

InstructionEntrySource.description: Instructions carried as a file at `SKILL.md`. The path is hashed into the carrying package's integrity chain, so editing the file changes the artifact digest by way of that chain.

InstructionInlineSource.description: Instructions written inline in Agent Program source rather than carried as a package file. There is no package path and no per-file digest to state: the instruction text is already inside the source bundle, so `source_bundle_digest` is the integrity anchor. Editing inline instructions changes the artifact digest through the source-bundle digest, not through a package file digest.
